name: Villa Mara
credit: Interior architecture, design & styling: Terraza Balear · Architecture: Revuelta y Stahn Arquitectos
overview: A 910 m² Mediterranean estate on the cliffs of Cala Llamp, Mallorca, surrounded by the sea and pine landscape.
concept: The interior and exterior are treated as a continuous living environment, with a restrained, almost monochrome palette and carefully layered textures that frame the surrounding views.
challenges: The design creates a calm relationship between the indoor living areas and the 350 m² of outdoor terraces and pool spaces, keeping the Mediterranean landscape central to the experience.
materials: The published project emphasizes layered natural textures, neutral tones, outdoor living furniture, and a cohesive relationship between interior and exterior spaces.

name: House with Japanese Kura
credit: Architecture & interior design: RON DESIGN / Articious Co., Ltd.
overview: A family residence that brings together a traditional Japanese storehouse, a new home, and an established garden setting.
concept: The project combines reinforced concrete and timber construction with traditional Japanese craft and contemporary living. Kyoto washi sliding doors and a sculpted plaster wall translate natural motifs into the interior.
challenges: The design brings together distinct generations of the family home and the inherited Kura while creating a contemporary residence with spaces for both family life and entertaining.
materials: Kyoto washi paper, timber, sculpted plaster, traditional craft details, shoji screens, and locally sourced materials.

name: Buro Happold London Workplace
overview: A 35,000-square-foot headquarters for Buro Happold in Shoreditch, organized across four floors of the Featherstone Building.
concept: The workplace balances open-plan work areas with collaboration and social spaces, using a strong material identity and a prominent mass-timber staircase to connect the floors.
challenges: The design supports hybrid working and a range of work styles while prioritizing employee wellbeing, inclusivity, and the integrity of the existing structure.
materials: Mass timber, exposed concrete, steel, planting, and a considered palette of workplace materials.
